title: docs(skills): objectstack-ui teaches at most one app per package, and that a module package may carry its own app
body:
Fixes #32587

This is the card's last item, Wanted item 2. Items 1, 3, 4 and 5 landed in PR 32616 (`cc543b4431`). The item waited on the ADR-0019 D3 amendment, which is on `main` as `958734cbac`.

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:`objectstack-ui` 的 `SKILL.md` App Navigation 一节不再说「更多受众永远不是第二个应用」,改教修订后的 ADR-0019 D3:每个包至多一个应用(应用包里写第二个,`defineStack` 拒绝);套件(应用包加它的模块)可以露出多个应用,模块包可以自带一个应用,挂在模块的包 id 下,模块停用时一起消失;受众共用同一个产品和同一批对象时,仍然是一个应用里用 `requiredPermissions` 把关的分组。评测用例 2 的题面和答案随之改一行。
- 为什么改:你裁决「改成 Salesforce 模式」后 ADR 已修订,但已发布的技能还在教「never a second app」,会继续让客户的 agent 以为应用不能拆。
- 风险与回滚:只改技能文字、一条评测和一个 changeset,不动运行时,也不动 token 天花板;新增文字靠同文件删三处不含规则的旁白付清。模块包「至多一个应用」目前只是声明、构建还不检查,所以技能既没说构建会拒绝,也没说模块可以带两个。回滚即 revert。
- 先看:① `skills/objectstack-ui/SKILL.md` App Navigation 改写的六行;② 同文件三处删减(见 Deletions);③ 评测用例 2 题面新增的「who work the same objects」。
- 两分钟验证:`node scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`,预期看到 `skills/objectstack-ui/SKILL.md 3814 / 3814 (+0)`,末行 `57 authored bundle file(s) within their ceilings`。
- 需要你做的:本 PR 触 `skills/**`,属 Tier H,保持 draft;席位的契约复核通过后,请你手动合并。

## What changes

- `skills/objectstack-ui/SKILL.md` § App Navigation. The paragraph that read "Exactly one App per `type: 'app'` package … More audiences are `requiredPermissions`-gated groups **inside** that one app, never a second app." now reads:

  > ⛔ **At most one App per package** (ADR-0019 (app-as-consumer-unit) D3): `defineStack` refuses a second in a `type: 'app'` package. A suite (an app package plus its modules) may surface more apps: a `type: 'module'` package may carry its own app, served under the module's package id and gone when the module is disabled. Audiences sharing one product and its objects stay `requiredPermissions`-gated groups **inside** one app.

  - The one-app-per-app-package rule is kept, with its enforcement named where it exists.
  - The module half is stated as the ADR states it, a rule per package. The text does not say the build refuses a module package with two apps (it does not yet), and does not present two apps in a module as allowed.
  - The words are the amendment's: app package, module, app, suite. `type: 'app'` is not renamed.
- `skills/objectstack-ui/evals/views-apps-actions-pages.json`, case 2. Its expected answer applied the old sentence to "a second app for the support team": always a gated group. The prompt now says the support team works the same objects, which is the fact that makes the gated group the answer under the amended rule, and the expected answer names the other arm (a support product with objects of its own would carry its app in its own module package). The `must_contain` and `must_not_contain` lists are unchanged. Case 17 (the Service app "from its own package") already agrees with the rule and is untouched.
- `.changeset/skills-ui-module-owned-apps.md`: `@objectstack/skills` patch.
- `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/navigation.md` is not in the diff: the rule fits in the `SKILL.md` paragraph.

### Taught claims and their sources (tree `cf648904`)

| Claim | Source on `main` |
|:--|:--|
| At most one app per package; a suite may surface more than one, each defined by a different package | `docs/adr/0019-app-as-consumer-unit.md`, D3 amendment note, "The rule." |
| `defineStack` refuses a second app in a `type: 'app'` package | `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` L2610-2619 (`validateSingleApp`), L3719 (`STACK_SINGLE_APP_VIOLATION`); pinned by `packages/spec/src/stack.test.ts` L1414 |
| No build refusal exists for other package types, so none is taught | `stack.zod.ts` L2611 (`manifest.type` other than `app` returns no finding); `stack.test.ts` L1424 ("does not constrain non-app package types") |
| An app is served under the id of the package that defines it | `ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/appRoute.ts` L46-58 (`appRouteSegment`, `matchAppBySegment`: the package id is the route key); `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-package-scope.ts` L58 (`resolveAppPackageIdKey`, the server's read by package id) |
| A disabled module's app is gone | `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-refusals.ts` L54 (`isItemOfDisabledPackage`); `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-list-reads.ts` L826 (the list read drops a disabled package's items, apps among them); `packages/runtime/src/domains/packages.ts` L800 (`isDisableableAppModule`, the disable door for a module of an installed app package) |
| A navigation item's `requiredPermissions` is enforced | `packages/spec/src/ui/app.zod.ts` L426 and L1274-1290 (unchanged teaching, kept) |

The card's own measurements on 18.3.0 (M2 and M11: an app in a module package builds, is served under the module's package id, and leaves the launcher and `/meta/app` when the module is disabled) agree with these readings.

### Deletions that pay for the new text (no ceiling moves, no re-wrap)

Token ratchet, `ceil(utf8 bytes / 4)` with the release-stamp line unpriced, measured by `node scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`:

| File | Before (`958734cb`) | After (`cf648904`) | Ceiling |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|

| `skills/objectstack-ui/rules/navigation.md` | 2179 | 2179 (untouched) | 2184 |

`scripts/check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs` is not in this diff. Each deletion is inside `SKILL.md`, and no lines were joined (the shortened lines are left short):

- Master-Detail Forms, "Line-item grid behaviors": the aside "(the QuickBooks / Stripe / NetSuite pattern)". A brand comparison, no rule. The behaviours it labelled are listed in the same sentence, and their rules stand in objectstack-data → Relationships → Inline Editing, which the sentence links.
- CRM UI Blueprint: the lead-in sentence "Use this CRM-style structure as the canonical UI assembly reference:" and its blank line. No rule. The heading and the table it introduced stand.
- Common Pitfalls, item 2: the two parentheticals "(it was silently dropped before protocol 17)" and "(the Studio designer relies on this)". History and rationale. The rules stand in the same item: `position` is not a widget key and the closed schema rejects it by name; `layout` is optional and an omitted one auto-flows.
- In the rewritten paragraph itself: "at load" and "never a second app" (the sentence this card rewords).

### Size readings (`skills/**` rule)

Net added lines across the `.md` files: +1 (`SKILL.md` +10 -9; budget +4). Eval: +2 -2, no net line (budget +6). The +44 bundle tokens are all in the eval fixture (3948 to 3992; measured, not ratcheted).

## Tests

No runtime code changes, so no unit test changes and no ablation (documentation). No `os:check` example block is touched.

The edited eval case holds the two rules the repository holds eval fixtures to, checked by a script over the fixture: every `must_contain` token of case 2 occurs in the case's own `expected_output` and in the bundle's markdown, and no `must_not_contain` entry occurs in its `expected_output`; the same holds for the untouched case 17. `ui/scripts/check-skill-eval-tokens.mjs` reads the `objectui` bundle only, so this is a hand check, not a gate reading.

`pnpm --filter @objectstack/skills build` at `cf648904`: `97 file(s) across 11 skill(s) copied from skills/** into dist/skills and read back byte-identical.`, lock `VERDICT command-exit 0`. The shipped copy carries the new paragraph (1 hit for "At most one App per package", 0 for "never a second app").

## Acceptance notes

- The module half of the rule is declared and not enforced: a module package with two apps builds today (`stack.test.ts` L1424 pins the same answer for a `driver` package). The check is card 32586. The skill states the rule only.
- Where a module's app lives is not checked by the build. Under the strict parse, in a package that defines at least one object, an app's own navigation entry naming an object the package does not define is refused unless the entry declares `requiresObject` (`stack.zod.ts` L5565 is the early return for a package with no object, L5714 the `requiresObject` pass). The skill sentence therefore says a module package "may carry its own app" and prescribes no placement. The eval's parenthetical names the shape that passes that check: the app sits in the module package that defines the objects it shows.
- "Gone when the module is disabled" describes what a disable does. Which packages an administrator may disable is narrower (`isDisableableAppModule`: a `type: 'module'` package that directly declares an installed `type: 'app'` package, outside the platform scopes), and is not taught here.
- `content/docs/ui/audience-based-interfaces.mdx` L22 still says "More audiences therefore never mean more apps". It is outside this card's file surface and is reported to the seat, not edited.
- Eval case 2 keeps `requiredPermissions` in `must_contain`. The assertions score the answer by string, so the prompt had to carry the fact that decides between the two arms; without it an answer that gives the support team a module-owned app would be right under the amended rule and still fail the token. The alternative, leaving the prompt and dropping the token, weakens the case.
